questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Australia because I wanted to attend a university with an international environment and the semesters in Australia often started in February which meant I had good time after my exams in Denmark to go to Australia.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of information and it is not always easy to find - and sometimes you don't even know that you should look for it. However, I find that University of Melbourne was really helpful and responded quickly to any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Melbourne held a pre-departure meeting where they told a lot of practical information. They also have a free airport pick-up which is nice to know about.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: OSHC was a bit confusing but ended up working out fine.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I stayed at International House which is just 1km off campus. I enjoyed it since it had a lot of postgraduates (and not just undergraduates) and there was the option to have your own studio apartment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I payed a bit extra to have my own kitchenette. Breakfast was included and you could also have a full catering package. There are also kitchens in the common areas.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is way more expensive than finding your own room in the city. However, I liked that I knew I had a place to stay and I loved the social life here.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed staying at International House but I don't feel like there were many other options available.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a bit confusing since you first apply for the classes you want to take and then a few weeks after you have to apply for the specific time you want to join the class. Most of my classes only had one option whereas others could decide between different times to have their classes. However, you can switch classes in the first 2 weeks of semester if you don't like the class (and there is an available spot in another class) which I thought was really nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Their Study Abroad team was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Know the dates for when to apply for classes and when to choose the specific time you want to attend class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took four MA courses. I mostly took classes in International Relations, and they were less theory-heavy than at UCPH. It is probably due to the fact that people studying a MA in IR doesn't need to hold a BA in IR.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some classes were more discussion-based but otherwise it was a combination of a quick lecture in the beginning and then discussions afterwards.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SOCI90026: Social Policy and Urban Problems
POLS90065: Cyberpolitics in International Relations
POLS90051: Technology and Power in World Politics
POLS90050: Terrorism and Insurgency

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend 'Technology and Power in World Politics' with Daniel McCarthy. Daniel is such a good teacher and I learned so much from the class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: To get your student visa, you have to pay for an OSHC which is a medical health insurance. However, I also payed to have a Danish travel insurance and therefore my expenses for insurance is quite high. However, I did have an accident where it was nice to have the Danish travel insurance to help with the process.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Generally Australia is quite expensive so I ended up using a bit more than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of opportunities and I tried out a few things but didn't stick with anything for the entire semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Anything from different sports to book club etc. There is also a surf society that hosts three surfing camps per semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In orientation week there will be some days where you can meet the different sports clubs and organisations and I would recommend to just walk around and have a chat with them and try out what you like.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Melbourne and Victoria and also the rest of Australia - but remember that Australia is really big, so it might be a good idea to do some research on what you really want to see, because time and money flies. I really enjoyed exploring Tasmania and Western Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just start a conversation, they are very open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Remember that Melbourne weather can get quite cold during autumn and winter. Bring warm clothes!
2) Check up on what happens in the city; there is always something going on. Night markets at Queen Victoria Market, exhibitions etc. 
3) Enjoy it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it and be openminded.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a new country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference to Denmark. It was hard sometimes to plan times to talk with friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
